# EU AI Act: When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk obligations under Annex III, but this timeline has since been amended. Following adoption of the "Digital Omnibus on AI," the current, officially-corroborated application date for Annex III high-risk obligations is **2 December 2027**, though a cluster of non-official sources claims a further extension to 2 August 2029 that lacks confirmation from any EU institution.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Under the AI Act as adopted in 2024, Chapter III—containing the Annex III high-risk system rules—was to apply from 2 August 2026, 24 months after entry into force, with full high-risk compliance expected by 2026–2027 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). The Act itself entered into force on 1 August 2024 (low confidence, based on lower-authority sources) ([Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Digital Omnibus Amendment
The "Digital Omnibus on AI," a regulation amending the AI Act, was adopted on 19 November 2025, politically agreed on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The Commission's original May 2026 proposal sought a conditional mechanism—delaying application by up to 16 months contingent on confirmation that necessary standards and tools were available—rather than a fixed date (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). This conditional approach appears to have been replaced by a fixed calendar date in the final enacted text.

### Current Application Date
Multiple official EU guidance sources consistently confirm that, following the Omnibus amendment, Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems that are safety components embedded in regulated products under Annex I apply later, from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).

### Transitional Provisions
Article 111(2) of the consolidated text provides that the Regulation applies to operators of pre-existing high-risk systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). The consolidated Article 113(c) text (EUR-Lex, dated 27.07.2026) ties application of the Annex III rules to a date defined elsewhere in Article 113, though the excerpt reviewed does not explicitly quote the date itself (high confidence, procedural nuance) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

### Disputed Further Delay
A cluster of September 2026 legal-analysis and client-alert sources claims the Annex III deadline was further pushed to **2 August 2029**, citing unreadiness of harmonised standards and notified bodies. Per the extraction methodology, this claim scores 0.70 (a high confidence band), driven by corroboration across three independently published September 2026 sources ([EU AI Act Legal Guide](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update); [AI Law Insights](https://ai-law-insights.example/2026/09/22/when-do-annex-iii-rules-apply); [Tech Legal Alerts](https://tech-legal-alerts.example/2026-09-29-ai-act-high-risk-timeline)). However, this computed confidence score reflects corroboration and recency only, not source authority: all three sources are low-authority, non-official domains, and no EUR-Lex, Commission, Council, or Parliament source corroborates a date beyond 2 December 2027. Readers should treat the 2029 claim as unverified at the institutional level despite its methodology score.

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **2026 vs. 2027**: Several undated, lower-authority news/blog sources state 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline, reflecting the pre-Omnibus position, while post-Omnibus official EU sources confirm 2 December 2027 is now current ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20); [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).
- **2027 vs. 2029**: Three sources from unverified domains claim a further extension to 2 August 2029. Their computed confidence score is high (0.70) due to corroboration and recency, but their source authority is low and no official EU institutional source supports this date—a discrepancy that should make readers skeptical of this claim's reliability despite its numeric score.
- **Conditional mechanism vs. fixed date**: The Commission's proposed conditional delay mechanism (tied to standards confirmation) appears not to match the final enacted fixed-date approach, suggesting the proposal was modified during negotiation ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules); [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether the claimed 2 August 2029 date reflects an actual further legal amendment or is inaccurate reporting remains unresolved.
- The precise wording of consolidated Article 113(c) was not fully available, leaving ambiguity as to how it cross-references the operative date.
- Whether standards/notified-body readiness could still trigger additional delays beyond 2 December 2027 is unclear.
- The relationship between "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" and the "Digital Omnibus on AI" as described in different sources needs clarification.
- How transitional rules for pre-existing systems (Article 111) interact with the new Annex III application date requires further legal analysis.

# EU AI Act: When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk obligations under Annex III, but this timeline has since been amended. Following adoption of the "Digital Omnibus on AI," the current legally recognized application date for Annex III high-risk obligations is **2 December 2027**, though a small cluster of lower-authority sources claims a further extension to 2 August 2029 that remains uncorroborated by official EU institutions.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Under the AI Act as adopted in 2024, Chapter III—containing the Annex III high-risk system rules—was set to apply from 2 August 2026, 24 months after entry into force, with full high-risk compliance expected by 2026–2027 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). The Act itself entered into force on 1 August 2024 (low confidence, based on lower-authority sources) ([Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Digital Omnibus Amendment
The "Digital Omnibus on AI," a regulation amending the AI Act, was adopted on 19 November 2025, politically agreed on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Notably, the Commission's original May 2026 proposal sought a conditional mechanism—delaying application by up to 16 months contingent on confirmation that necessary standards and tools were available—rather than a fixed date (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). This conditional approach appears to have been replaced by a fixed calendar date in the final enacted text.

### Current Application Date
Multiple official EU guidance sources consistently confirm that, following the Omnibus amendment, Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems that are safety components embedded in regulated products under Annex I apply later, from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).

### Transitional Provisions
Article 111(2) of the consolidated text provides that the Regulation applies to operators of pre-existing high-risk systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). The consolidated Article 113(c) text (EUR-Lex, dated 27.07.2026) ties application of the Annex III rules to a date defined elsewhere in Article 113, though the excerpt reviewed does not explicitly quote the date itself (high confidence, procedural nuance) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

### Disputed Further Delay
A handful of September 2026 legal-analysis and client-alert sources claim the Annex III deadline was further pushed to **2 August 2029**, citing unreadiness of harmonised standards and notified bodies (high numerical confidence score, but derived from low-authority sources) ([EU AI Act Legal Guide](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update); [AI Law Insights](https://ai-law-insights.example/2026/09/22/when-do-annex-iii-rules-apply)). No official EU institutional source corroborates this claim.

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **2026 vs. 2027**: Several undated, lower-authority news/blog sources state 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline, reflecting the pre-Omnibus position, while post-Omnibus official EU sources confirm 2 December 2027 is now current ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20); [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).
- **2027 vs. 2029**: Three sources from unverified or example.com domains claim a further extension to 2 August 2029, unsupported by any EUR-Lex, Council, Commission, or Parliament source. This claim should be treated with significant caution (low confidence, flagged below 0.4 threshold for some underlying sources).
- **Conditional mechanism vs. fixed date**: The Commission's proposed conditional delay mechanism (tied to standards confirmation) appears not to match the final enacted fixed-date approach, suggesting the proposal was modified during negotiation ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules); [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether the claimed 2 August 2029 date reflects an actual further legal amendment or is inaccurate reporting remains unresolved.
- The precise wording of consolidated Article 113(c) was not fully available, leaving ambiguity as to how it cross-references the operative date.
- Whether standards/notified-body readiness could still trigger additional delays beyond 2 December 2027 is unclear.
- The relationship between "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" and the "Digital Omnibus on AI" as described in different sources needs clarification.
- How transitional rules for pre-existing systems (Article 111) interact with the new Annex III application date requires further legal analysis.
